name: PA-05
label: Safe D

key_factors: Challenger raised under $10,000 versus Scanlon's $1.26 million, with no outside spending on either side
District's D+15 partisan lean favors the incumbent party by a wide structural margin
Scanlon is a running incumbent with cash on hand, adding a consistent incumbency edge

model.rationale: The money gap is nearly absolute, the district leans Democratic by fifteen points, and an entrenched incumbent faces a challenger without the resources to compete, so every available signal points to a comfortable Democratic hold.
model.watch: A late infusion of outside Republican spending or a dramatic national shift toward Republicans could narrow the margin, though nothing in the current evidence suggests either.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Incumbent Mary Gay Scanlon (D) is running.

overview:
Pennsylvania's 5th District, anchored in Delaware County and Philadelphia's western suburbs, leans Democratic by about fifteen points. Mary Gay Scanlon, first elected in 2018, seeks re-election with more than $1.2 million raised and roughly $460,000 on hand. Republican Nicholas Manganaro has raised under $10,000, leaving him without resources for advertising or meaningful outreach, and no outside groups have invested on either side.

No public general-election polls cover the race and rating houses have not weighed in, so the assessment rests on the district's partisan baseline, the incumbent's structural advantages, and the lopsided money contest. Prediction markets price the Democratic candidate near 98 percent. With the national environment also tilting favorable for Democrats, the challenger would need a shift far larger than anything current evidence indicates to make this competitive.
